Donald Trump was the 45th president of the United States serving from 2017 to 2021 after defeating Hillary Clinton.
As a businessman and real estate mogul Trump built his career in New York City developing iconic properties like Trump Tower.
Trump's America First foreign policy prioritized American interests and reshaped international relations during his presidency.
He was impeached twice by the House of Representatives making him the only president to achieve this distinction.
Make America Great Again became Trump's signature slogan that energized his political base across the country.
Trump appointed three conservative justices to the Supreme Court reshaping the judiciary for generations to come.
The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 was Trump's major legislative achievement reducing corporate tax rates significantly.
Trump's business career included ownership of casinos hotels and golf courses around the world.
His reality television show The Apprentice made Trump a household name before his political career began.
Trump faced two impeachment trials first over Ukraine pressure and second over the January 6th Capitol riot.

Donald Trump was born in Queens New York in 1946 and attended Fordham University before transferring to Wharton.

He withdrew the United States from the Paris Climate Agreement citing unfair burdens on American workers.
Trump's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic became a central point of criticism during his presidency.
The Abraham Accords brokered by Trump normalized relations between Israel and several Arab nations.
Trump frequently used Twitter to communicate directly with the public bypassing traditional media channels.
His family including Ivanka Donald Jr and Eric played significant roles in his business and administration.
Trump survived two assassination attempts during the 2024 campaign demonstrating his resilience to supporters.
He promoted deregulation across multiple industries reducing what he called burdensome government oversight.
Trump's tariff policies targeted China specifically aiming to reduce the trade deficit with that nation.

Trump's border policies including family separation generated significant controversy and legal challenges nationwide.
He moved the US embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem fulfilling a longstanding campaign promise.
Trump's rhetoric often focused on law and order themes resonating with voters concerned about crime.
His net worth fluctuated significantly throughout his career with Forbes tracking his business successes and failures.
Trump's electoral college victory in 2016 came despite losing the popular vote to Hillary Clinton.
He frequently clashed with the media coining the term fake news to describe unfavorable coverage.
Trump's Space Force was established as the sixth branch of the US military during his administration.

Trump's golf courses became frequent venues for his diplomacy and leisure time as president.
He criticized NATO allies for not meeting defense spending targets threatening to withdraw US support.

Trump's legal challenges included investigations into his business practices and campaign activities.
His speaking style featured repetition and simple language that made his message accessible to many.

Trump's energy policy promoted fossil fuel production including opening federal lands to drilling.
He withdrew from the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade agreement on his fourth day in office.
Trump's children remained active in his business empire while he served as president.
His post-presidency influence over the Republican Party remained substantial through 2026 and beyond.
